stories.title: "The beginning of a new scientific paradigm": Zuckerberg's Biohub, U.S. and Google build virtual cell

sources.title: Google invests millions in Mark Zuckerberg’s efforts to create a ‘virtual cell’
sources.text: The Zuckerberg-backed Biohub will use the investment to create AI datasets that help researchers ‘ask, predict, and answer biological questions digitally.’ The Zuckerberg-backed Biohub will use the investment to create AI datasets that help researchers ‘ask, predict, and answer biological questions digitally.’ Google DeepMind, Meta, and AI drug discovery startup Isomorphic Labs are jointly investing $300 million into an initiative to create a “virtual cell” that researchers can use to combat disease, as reported earlier by Reuters . The project is led by Biohub, a nonprofit biomedical research organization founded by Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan. It comes as part of a $1.8 billion “Virtual Biology” initiative to build AI datasets that could allow researchers to “ask, predict, and answer biological questions digitally.” Founded in 2016 , Biohub aims to prevent and cure diseases through the creation of a “high-accuracy predictive model of the cell ” that researchers can use to carry out simulations. To support this effort, the US Department of Energy will invest more than $500 million over the next five years, while the National Institutes of Health will contribute datasets , repositories, and knowledge bases stemming from previous federal investment totalling over $500 million. “An accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery by enabling scientists to perform experiments digitally,” Alex Rives, Biohub’s head of science, says in the press release. “The creation of a virtual cell is one of the most important challenges for the next era of science. It will require coordinated data generation efforts at a national and international scale, which is why these partners are coming together.” Update, October 7th: Clarified that Google, Meta, and Isomorphic Labs are investing in Biohub’s Virtual Biology initiative.

sources.title: Muse launches on the iPad
sources.text: Meta’s AI agent now properly supports the iPad’s larger screen and recent improvements to multitasking. Meta’s AI agent now properly supports the iPad’s larger screen and recent improvements to multitasking. After launching nearly a month ago and spending several weeks as the top free app in Apple’s App Store, the latest update to Meta’s Muse iOS app introduces native support for the iPad. A Mac version of Meta’s agentic AI tool (designed to compete with OpenClaw, ChatGPT’s Dots, and Grok Bot) was released about a week after the original mobile version debuted expanding its usefulness to desktop tasks like organizing files. The new iPad version should function similar to Muse on iPhones, but better take advantage of the extra screen real estate and iPadOS’ better multitasking capabilities . The newly added iPad support is limited to just a one line mention at the bottom of the release notes for the latest version of Muse alongside several other updates for the iPhone version too. These include the ability to connect Muse to additional software tools like Canva, Dropbox, Figma, QuickBooks, GitHub, Zoom, Asana, and Klaviyo, and new connectors for apps like Granola and Notion. The new updates target small business owners with the option to give Muse a business goal which the agent will use to autonomously plan marketing, client pitches, and developing “new product pages.” While it took Meta 15 years to release a dedicated version of Instagram for the iPad , the faster turnaround for Muse properly supporting Apple’s tablets is a clear indicator of the company’s strong support for its AI initiatives. Meta also recently announced a standalone Tamagotchi-like device called the Muse Charm that will run the AI agent without the need for a smartphone, and it’s working to bring Muse to its smart glasses .

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: Meta’s Muse launches on iPad just a month after its mobile debut
sources.text: If there’s any doubt about how seriously Meta is taking AI, here’s a new signal: The company on Wednesday announced that its Muse assistant is now available in a dedicated iPad app . That’s a milestone it took Instagram some 15 years to reach, despite constant user demand. Muse, meanwhile, hit the iPad just a month after launching on iPhone. (To be fair, it may not be as difficult to bring something like Muse to iPad, given its text-heavy interface, where image and video resolution and formatting matter less.) Since launching on iOS and Android on September 8, Muse has topped 6.6 million installs, according to estimates from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. The app, which is now one of dozens of consumer-facing AI agents, lets users connect their accounts to stay on top of email, meetings, bills, and more, and to complete tasks like booking reservations, ordering groceries, setting goals, and making purchases. To make that work, Meta has been adding partners in the effort, which appear in Muse as “connectors.” Users can add and sign in to them selectively, depending on which parts of their online life they’re comfortable letting an AI agent handle. With the iPad release, Meta has updated this list with several of its newer additions , including connectors aimed at small businesses, like Asana, Canva, Dropbox, Figma, QuickBooks, GitHub, Klaviyo, and Zoom, as well as connectors for Meta ad accounts. It also added Notion and Granola. In addition, Meta recently announced more retail partners, like Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Walmart, and Wayfair. These allow the agent to shop those retailers’ sites and complete transactions on users’ behalf. Because this technology is still new, these experiences can still run into issues as websites mistake agents for bots and block their access . On Tuesday, Meta announced that it’s working with industry partners on a technological solution to this problem in the form of an open standard that would allow personal AI agents to identify themselves to businesses. stories.title: ChatGPT is getting a lot more visual, with the launch of a new interface
stories.summary: OpenAI is launching a new user interface that will bring interactive visuals to ChatGPT.

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: ChatGPT is getting a lot more visual, with the launch of a new interface
sources.text: ChatGPT is about to get a lot more visual, thanks to a new feature that OpenAI calls Intelligent UI. The new interface, which is being rolled out Wednesday with a new GPT-6 model, will integrate a significant amount of visuals into users’ conversations. OpenAI says many of those visuals will be interactive. In other words, instead of just flat, cartoonish pictures, the chatbot will frequently include things like tappable buttons, a customized calculator for a specific task, interactive charts, editable graphs, and other elements the user can work with directly. The big goal here, according to OpenAI, is to make “learning complex topics easier.” It may also make ChatGPT friendlier and more accessible and help bring in a wider audience, though OpenAI didn’t say so directly. In a call with journalists, OpenAI staff gave a brief demonstration of Intelligent UI’s capabilities, showing how the new chatbot can instantly whip up various diagrams and visuals that help users understand more abstract topics. Aarush Selvan, a product manager at the company, said that while “ChatGPT has predominantly been a text-based interface,” the company really wants to help users “get things done — from everyday things like planning a recipe or a trip or even trying to learn something — the most helpful answers aren’t just text.” Selvan gave the example of a college student wanting to know how an airplane wing functions. He asked ChatGPT to “explore how an airplane wing generates lift” and the chatbot quickly spun up a number of diagrams designed to show how planes stay in the air. Other examples from the company included things like visuals for recipes, a diagram explaining bicycle mechanics, a map for a multi-day hiking excursion, a personal savings calculator, and more. This new feature will be customizable. As with other aspects of ChatGPT’s personality, if users don’t want so many visuals in their responses, they’ll be able to dial them back. Intelligent UI rolls out globally with GPT-6 for Pro, Plus, Business, and Enterprise users, and arrives Thursday for users of the free and lower-cost Go tiers. sources.name: Canaltech
sources.title: ChatGPT passa por transformação e libera nova interface visual para todos
sources.text: A OpenAI começou a liberar o Intelligent UI , nova interface do ChatGPT que transforma as respostas do chatbot em experiências visuais e interativas. A novidade acompanha o lançamento do GPT-6 e adiciona recursos, como gráficos editáveis, calculadoras personalizadas, mapas, diagramas explicativos e botões clicáveis, às conversas. Com a atualização, o ChatGPT amplia as respostas para além dos tradicionais blocos de texto e adapta a apresentação ao tipo de tarefa . Uma pergunta sobre um assunto complexo pode resultar em um diagrama interativo e um pedido envolvendo cálculos pode gerar uma ferramenta específica para resolver o problema. A tecnologia também pode criar mapas para planejar viagens, comparadores de assentos em avião ou combinações de roupas e jogos retrô inspirados em clássicos, como Snake, Breakout e Pong. A proposta da OpenAI é facilitar o aprendizado e tarefas do dia a dia sem que o usuário precise sair da conversa para encontrar uma ferramenta adequada. O sistema combina diferentes componentes visuais e monta a interface enquanto a resposta é criada. Entre os exemplos apresentados pela empresa estão diagramas para explicar a sustentação de uma asa de avião ou a anatomia de uma lesma, além de calculadoras para dividir contas e simuladores de planejamento financeiro. A experiência também pode ser ajustada de acordo com a preferência do usuário. Quem quiser uma interação mais próxima do formato tradicional pode reduzir a quantidade de elementos visuais gerados pelo ChatGPT nas configurações. A OpenAI também afirma que o GPT-6 recebeu melhorias de velocidade, pesquisa na web e segurança, com maior resistência a tentativas de burlar as regras e melhor capacidade de reconhecer quando não tem informações ou ferramentas suficientes para responder. Sim. O Intelligent UI começou a ser liberado globalmente junto ao GPT-6 para usuários dos planos ChatGPT Pro, Plus, Business e Enterprise. No Enterprise, a disponibilidade depende das configurações definidas pelos administradores da organização. Para quem usa os planos Free e Go, a novidade chega a partir da próxima quinta-feira . Nos planos Pro, Plus, Business e Enterprise, a experiência é alimentada pelo GPT-6 Sol e nas contas Free e Go utilizam o GPT-6 Luna. Vale ressaltar que a atualização fica restrita à aba de Chat do ChatGPT e não altera os modelos utilizados nos produtos Work e Codex. Se você gostou do conteúdo, talvez também se interesse por conferir “ 8 formas inesperadas de usar o ChatGPT no dia a dia ”.
